title: One of 16 ozone nutrition checks failed a covariance bound under common-sample assumptions in a 2024 extract
abstract: We tested whether unknown covariance can explain nutrition-index mean gaps in a public invertebrate extract. Four matched contexts from one US paper gave 16 necessary covariance checks. All eight growth checks and seven of eight digestion-conversion checks passed. One check required a correlation of -1.168 under exact, unadjusted common-sample assumptions. Independent changes of up to 0.474% in each of three means remove that flag with fixed standard deviations. This is a conditional diagnostic, not proof of source error. Complete sets from other regions and periods were absent under the selection rule. We give a proof, code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval instructions. Source records remain external. We do not test climate or weather effects.

display.caption: Required correlations in 16 necessary common-sample checks. Values outside minus one to plus one fail the bound. Checks share four contexts in one paper.

citations.reason: Extends its open covariance explanation with necessary moment bounds. No derived record table or code was reused.
